about.process.build.body: Prototype quickly, then connect it to the real APIs, data and workflows instead of hiding the complexity behind a UI.
about.process.discover.body: Clarify the user, the business rule, the integration boundary, the risk and what the output has to be — then write it down as scope.
about.process.evaluate.body: Test, compare regressions, decide whether it is release-ready, deliver it, and improve it from how it behaves in real use.
about.process.evaluate.title: Evaluate, ship and iterate
about.process.title: Discover → scope → build → integrate → evaluate → ship.
about.profile.approach: That is where discovery and technical scoping do the real work: naming the users, the business rules, the integration boundaries and the success criteria, then getting to a prototype fast enough that the conversation can continue against something real. I care about what the system actually does, not only whether the interface looks convincing.
about.profile.evidence: In 2026, SINAMA became my strongest evidence that AI behavior can be evaluated instead of guessed at, and Atölye Joyday remains the real-business example of owning a customer-facing product end to end. Merge Rush: Tiny Factory carries the product-engineering breadth behind both.
about.profile.experience: At CBOT, I worked on enterprise conversational-AI projects involving chatbot QA, stabilization, channel configuration, flow restructuring and an insurance-claims intake POC. Project-based AI evaluation work added structured review of LLM responses, reasoning, code and multimodal outputs.
about.profile.title: The part I like is the beginning, when nobody can say yet what the system has to do.

mergeRush.cover.alt: Merge Rush Tiny Factory portfolio cover
mergeRush.designGoal.body: The player should immediately understand drop → merge → order, then discover a second layer of larger footprints, staged board unlocks, repair progression, combos and failure pressure.
mergeRush.designGoal.title: Readable in seconds, deeper over the full run.
mergeRush.engineering.deadlock: The run checks whether legal placements or merges remain instead of treating a visually crowded board as automatically terminal.
mergeRush.engineering.footprints: Higher-tier pieces use 2×1, 1×2 and 2×2 footprints. Placement, movement, merge, delivery and deadlock checks are footprint-aware.
mergeRush.engineering.preview: Drag/drop validates the destination before committing board state, keeping visual feedback and logical placement aligned.
mergeRush.engineering.repair: Wrong-action damage and successful-delivery repair create a second failure/recovery loop after the main Factory Run.
mergeRush.loop.drop: Drop parts from the next queue
mergeRush.loop.energy: Earn score, combo and Repair Energy
mergeRush.loop.unlock: Unlock more board space and higher pressure
mergeRush.platform.adapters: Local and YouTube adapters isolate host-platform behavior from core gameplay.
mergeRush.platform.boot: Boot/loading architecture accounts for lifecycle interruptions and production platform behavior.
mergeRush.platform.lifecycle: Platform lifecycle and readiness coordination avoid scattering host callbacks through scene code.
mergeRush.platform.save: Save, audio and localization concerns use dedicated abstractions rather than being embedded in GameScene.
mergeRush.qa.report: no visible clipping, overlap, stretched art, broken margins or unreadable primary copy was reported in the four required aspect-ratio classes during the documented visual pass.
mergeRush.repo.private: The development repository remains private while the product is being iterated.
mergeRush.stage.assembly.body: More board capacity arrives as order pressure grows.
mergeRush.stage.core.body: The final restoration stage anchors the high-tier end of the run.
mergeRush.stage.emergency.body: Compact starting area makes early placement matter.
mergeRush.stage.mid.body: Mid-run restoration becomes a visible pacing checkpoint.
mergeRush.stage.robotics.body: Larger items and board planning become more important.
mergeRush.status.implemented: Merge loop, timed orders, restoration progression, staged board unlocks, multi-cell footprints, deadlock-aware placement, Factory Run, Endless mode, responsive layouts and platform architecture foundations.
mergeRush.status.refining: Gameplay pacing, retention, balancing, final production polish, public playable packaging and the final media/proof pack.
mergeRush.status.title: Implemented systems are separated from the work still being refined.

sinama.productQuestion: Is this agent version reliable enough to release?
sinama.readiness.body: Execution errors and HIGH/CRITICAL failures or regressions can block release. MEDIUM/LOW issues or missing baseline context can warn. Healthy evidence can produce READY.
sinama.regression.body: Runs can be marked as baselines and compared across agent versions. The product distinguishes improved, stable and regressed behavior, including new, resolved and persistent failures.
